title: Ensure verification of signed commits for new changes before merging
description: Git commit authorship is self-asserted: anyone who can push can claim to be anyone. Azure Repos cannot verify a signature itself — it has no signature policy, no server-side hook, and the commits it creates on merge are unsigned — so the only enforcement is a service that verifies every commit of a pull request and posts a status that a Required status policy waits for.
remediation: Run a service or pipeline that verifies the signature of every commit in a pull request and posts a pull request status, then require it: Project settings -> Repositories -> <repository> -> Policies -> Branch Policies -> <default branch> -> Status checks -> +, Policy requirement Required, "Apply by default", no path filter. Name that status in signatureStatusChecks in azure-devops-bench's config ("genre/name" or "name"); until one is named this control fails, because nothing else on Azure Repos can verify a signature. Allow only "Rebase and fast-forward" merges (Limit merge types), since the merge and squash commits Azure DevOps creates are unsigned.
fixSummary: Require a signature-verifying status at Project settings -> Repositories -> <repo> -> Policies.
